concepts.name: Elements of design
concepts.summary: Recognise and name the basic elements: line, shape, color, texture, space and form.

concepts.name: Principles of design
concepts.summary: Name the core principles such as balance, contrast, repetition, alignment, proximity and emphasis.

concepts.name: Alignment and proximity
concepts.summary: Explain how aligning items and grouping related items close together creates order and shows relationships.

concepts.name: Visual hierarchy
concepts.summary: Understand that size, weight and contrast guide the viewer to read some items before others.

concepts.name: Typeface categories
concepts.summary: Distinguish serif, sans serif, script and display typefaces and describe their general character.

concepts.name: Color wheel and hue
concepts.summary: Understand hue, primary, secondary and complementary colors and how they relate on the color wheel.

concepts.name: White space
concepts.summary: Explain that empty space gives content room to breathe and improves clarity.

misconceptions.text: Empty space is wasted and should be filled with content or decoration.
Using more fonts, colors and effects makes a design more interesting and professional.
Design is just about making things look pretty rather than communicating clearly.

concepts.name: Grid-based layout
concepts.summary: Build a layout using columns, margins and gutters so elements align consistently.

concepts.name: Type size and weight contrast
concepts.summary: Create a clear typographic hierarchy for headings, subheads and body text using size, weight and style.

concepts.name: Line length and leading
concepts.summary: Set comfortable line spacing and line length so body text is easy to read.

concepts.name: Font pairing
concepts.summary: Combine two typefaces with enough contrast and a shared feel, limiting the number used.

concepts.name: Color schemes
concepts.summary: Build palettes using monochromatic, analogous, complementary and neutral-plus-accent schemes.

concepts.name: Text and background contrast
concepts.summary: Choose text and background combinations with enough value contrast to be legible.

concepts.name: Balance types
concepts.summary: Distinguish symmetrical and asymmetrical balance and apply each to arrange visual weight.

concepts.name: Repetition and consistency
concepts.summary: Reuse styles, spacing and colors to unify a multi-element design such as a slide deck.

misconceptions.text: Any two colors that look good individually will work well together in a design.
Centering all text and elements is the safest way to get a balanced layout.
Bright, saturated colors on a colored background are always readable if they are different hues.

concepts.name: Gestalt grouping principles
concepts.summary: Analyse how similarity, closure, continuity and figure-ground shape how viewers perceive and group elements.

concepts.name: Reading patterns and flow
concepts.summary: Analyse how viewers' eyes move through a layout and arrange content to lead them along an intended path.

concepts.name: Focal point creation
concepts.summary: Establish a single clear focal point using scale, isolation, color or contrast.

concepts.name: Color meaning and context
concepts.summary: Analyse how color associations vary by audience and culture and fit palette choices to message and purpose.

concepts.name: Value and saturation control
concepts.summary: Adjust value and saturation to build depth, emphasis and a cohesive palette.

concepts.name: Composition frameworks
concepts.summary: Use rule of thirds, diagonals and similar frameworks to position elements in a composition.

concepts.name: Kerning, tracking and spacing
concepts.summary: Diagnose and correct spacing between letters, words and lines for display and body text.

concepts.name: Accessible color and type
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs for contrast ratios, color-blind safety and minimum text sizes.

misconceptions.text: Following the rule of thirds or golden ratio guarantees a good composition.
Each color has a universal meaning that works the same for every audience.
Making everything bold or large ensures that the important message gets noticed.

concepts.name: Design critique method
concepts.summary: Evaluate a design against its goals and audience, giving reasoned feedback rather than personal taste.

concepts.name: Brief-driven design decisions
concepts.summary: Derive layout, type and color choices from the objective, audience and context in a brief.

concepts.name: Rule-breaking with intent
concepts.summary: Judge when breaking alignment, balance or hierarchy conventions strengthens a message and when it harms it.

concepts.name: Systematic type scales
concepts.summary: Analyse and build type scales with consistent ratios that hold across sizes and formats.

concepts.name: Imagery and text integration
concepts.summary: Analyse how images, cropping, overlays and text interact to support or undermine legibility and message.

concepts.name: Cognitive load in visuals
concepts.summary: Evaluate how density, number of elements and competing cues affect comprehension, and simplify accordingly.

concepts.name: Adapting across formats
concepts.summary: Adapt one design to varied sizes and media such as poster, social post and slide while preserving hierarchy.

misconceptions.text: Design critique is about whether the critic personally likes the design.
Once the rules are learned, a good designer follows them strictly in every situation.
A layout that works at poster size can simply be scaled down for social media or slides.

concepts.name: Design systems thinking
concepts.summary: Create a coherent system of type, color, spacing and layout rules that scales across many pieces and designers.

concepts.name: Concept-driven visual language
concepts.summary: Originate a distinctive visual concept and language that expresses a message beyond conventional solutions.

concepts.name: Evaluating design effectiveness
concepts.summary: Judge a design's success using evidence such as user testing and outcome metrics, not just aesthetics.

concepts.name: Historical and cultural context
concepts.summary: Evaluate how movements such as Modernism, Swiss style and Bauhaus and cultural norms shape and justify choices.

concepts.name: Ethical and inclusive design
concepts.summary: Assess designs for misleading emphasis, exclusion and stereotyping, and adapt them for diverse audiences.

concepts.name: Synthesising constraints and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Resolve competing demands of brand, budget, medium, accessibility and message into a justified design solution.

concepts.name: Mentoring and critique leadership
concepts.summary: Develop critique frameworks and guidance that raise the quality of others' work and align teams on direction.

misconceptions.text: A design system is only a style guide that removes creativity.
Award-winning or visually striking designs are necessarily the most effective ones.
Good design is universal and independent of cultural and historical context.
